title: Worksheet — Real Numbers (Class 10 CBSE Mathematics)
instructions: Attempt all 10 questions. Show ALL working. Total time: 50 minutes.

questions.question: In Euclid's lemma a = bq + r, the remainder r satisfies:
HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b for any two positive integers a, b.
Use Euclid's algorithm to find HCF(420, 130). Show every step.
Find HCF and LCM of 24 and 36 by prime factorisation. Verify HCF × LCM = product.
Find HCF and LCM of 12, 15 and 21.
questions.answer: 12 = 2²·3. 15 = 3·5. 21 = 3·7. HCF = 3 (only prime common to all). LCM = 2²·3·5·7 = 420.

questions.question: Without performing the division, decide whether each has a TERMINATING or NON-TERMINATING decimal: (a) 7/8, (b) 13/3125, (c) 23/30, (d) 64/455.
questions.answer: (a) 7/8: 8 = 2³ — terminates. (b) 13/3125: 3125 = 5⁵ — terminates. (c) 23/30: 30 = 2·3·5 — has 3 — NOT terminating. (d) 64/455: 455 = 5·7·13 — has 7 and 13 — NOT terminating.

questions.question: Prove that √2 is irrational.
questions.answer: Assume √2 is rational; then √2 = p/q in lowest terms (HCF(p, q) = 1, q ≠ 0). Squaring: p² = 2q². So p² is even, hence p is even (an odd integer's square is odd). Write p = 2k. Then p² = 4k² = 2q², so q² = 2k². So q² is even, hence q is even. But then both p and q have factor 2, contradicting HCF(p, q) = 1. So √2 is IRRATIONAL.

questions.question: Three bells start ringing together at 7 a.m. They ring at intervals of 12, 15 and 18 minutes. (i) When will they next ring together? (ii) How many times will they all ring together in the next 6 hours?
questions.answer: (i) Need LCM(12, 15, 18). 12 = 2²·3; 15 = 3·5; 18 = 2·3². LCM = 2²·3²·5 = 180 min = 3 hours. Next together at 7 + 3 = 10 a.m. (ii) After 7 a.m., they ring together at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m. (within the next 6 hours, until 1 p.m.). So 2 times.
